speaker: The Chairman
text: Head I, Ministry of Social and Family Development.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Singapore's economic structure is now closer to that of a mature economy.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It, therefore, speaks volumes about the caring nature of the People's Action Party (PAP) Government that, despite harder-to-achieve growth, significant additional resources have been provided consistently to MSF – to build strong families, foster a caring society and build resilience among Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: MSF has done much with the additional resources provided.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In the past, Singaporeans could progress up the socio-economic ladder by working hard.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Today, economic growth is modest and climbing the social mobility ladder has become more challenging.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Forward Singapore (Forward SG) report found that rising inequality and slowing social mobility could fracture social cohesion.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How does MSF intend to tackle social mobility challenges, so that we can continue to foster a society where no one is left behind?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How will MSF improve its suite of assistance schemes, beyond adjusting for inflation, so that they remain adequate in helping lower-income families?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: ComLink is a good programme, but we need to move beyond assistance to empowerment.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We need to address service gaps brought about by siloed programmes and move from being programme-centric to be more client-centric.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How can we incentivise lower-income families to take on careers that have a long-term wage growth trajectory, rather than defaulting to gig work?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The success of ComLink can be attributed to the many men and women who work tirelessly behind the scenes to bring comfort, support and hope to those facing difficult circumstances.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Our social workers are the backbone of our community, providing essential services to those who are struggling with poverty, homelessness, abuse, mental health issues and more.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It takes a special kind of person to do this demanding and often emotionally draining work and I would like to take this opportunity to pay tribute to all our social workers out there in the frontline.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond assistance programmes, we must continue to promote active volunteerism and generous giving.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Members here would know of countless dedicated grassroots volunteers who work hard, delivering food and daily essentials to seniors, serving as befrienders and giving to local social assistance programmes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Loosely translated, it means that, "we can all contribute in ways that we can, be it in terms of time, talent or treasures".

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In this regard, corporate donors and patrons also play important roles in volunteerism.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: They provide the valuable resources, fundings that enable volunteers to deliver aid to vulnerable families.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We can do more to deepen philanthropy by corporates.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: According to various surveys conducted throughout the years, volunteerism rates in Singapore has gone through ups and downs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Some 20 years ago, less than 10% of Singaporeans volunteered.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What is the MSF's plan to encourage all segments of society to play their part in building a kinder, more generous Singapore?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Forward SG report found that Singaporeans want a resilient and united Singapore.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As we forge our shared future together, we must strengthen our social compact, so that we can ride through the inevitable challenges that will come our way, challenges that can impact, threaten our unity.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Together with the 4G team, I am confident that we can continue to make Singapore our best home for our children and our children's children.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Chairman, I have spoken in this House on numerous occasions on how families are the bedrock of our society.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Families are our first lines of support, providing us love, care and refuge when we need them the most.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: In addition to providing marriage and parenting resources for families, we can do more to promote marriage and reduce divorces.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Every year, the Families for Life Council, Registry of Marriages (ROM) and Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) jointly organise a Golden Jubilee Wedding Celebration event, for couples celebrating at least 50 years of marriage.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: This is a great event to celebrate marriages.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can we organise more of such events to celebrate periodic marriage milestones, such as 10 years, 20 years, 30 years?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: For our most vulnerable families, FSCs play a critical role in helping them deal with social and emotional issues.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: The work that our social work practitioners do at the FSC often goes unseen, but they are vital, nonetheless.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Mr Chairman, restorative justice is a process of healing from the harm caused by another person's actions.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This process brings together everyone who were affected to dialogue, problem solve and rebuild their lives and relationships.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Based on the premise that every individual has worth and needs to be regarded with dignity, it aims to establish social equality in relationships.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When spousal violence happens, it violates the intimate relationship, resulting in harm to self and others.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Counselling for spousal violence normally involves the spouses.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But spousal violence does not affect the spouses alone.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It also has negative impact on the well-being of the children and other family members.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Therefore, there is a need to address spousal violence in the context of needs of affected parties arising from the violence and to identify the obligations required by the different stakeholders to address the issue.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The restorative justice approach, therefore, involves children and other family members in the counselling process.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Restorative justice seeks to restore victims, perpetrators, and families by addressing the harm caused by violence and seeking accountability and support to foster healing.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Numerous countries have adopted restorative approaches, including Canada, the United Kingdom (UK), Australia, New Zealand, Norway, United States (US) and Japan.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I understand that in Singapore this approach is also adopted with respect to juvenile offenders.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the restorative justice process currently adopted in counselling sessions involving cases of spousal violence?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If not, would the Minister consider offering this as an option?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman, as we work towards fostering a family-friendly Singapore, it is important to leverage a whole-of-society approach to nurture and strengthen our family support systems.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One of the key themes in the Forward SG conversation and Budget 2024 is also about doing more to help support families through every stage of life.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A holistic approach is indeed crucial to strengthen family resilience, especially in the early marriages stage, as statistics show that Singapore has the highest proportion of divorces occurring in the first five to 10 years of marriage.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the same time, we also need to be inclusive of different family structures, such as single-parent families, blended families and families with special needs.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this regard, I would like to ask how MSF will tailor the Family for Life initiative to also cater for the unique challenges of these different family structures.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I am so appreciative and thankful for the many individuals who have given their best to work in the social service sector.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: For over 30 years, I have engaged with the many who serve with passion and dedication.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In the spectrum of services, the work is often very challenging.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: The needs of today as we embark on our new social compact will require additional people with commitment, care and compassion.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We also need to take care of those already serving in the social services whether in their early, mid or late career stages.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Remuneration needs to keep pace with other sectors.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Career progression, recognising and acknowledging talent will contribute to ensuring everyone can give their best.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Chairman, I am happy to learn that children enrolled in Government-supported preschools will enjoy lower fees from 2025.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Lower-income families with non-working mothers will also receive higher preschool subsidies, on par with subsidies enjoyed by working mothers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: MSF has done much to improve accessibility of preschools.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: This is a welcome move for young couples, who are often financially sandwiched, as they care for their children and elderly parents.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: One segment that I am particularly concerned about are children from lower-income households.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can MSF update whether we have narrowed this gap?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Beyond financial subsidies, what are MSF's plans to work with the community and social service agencies to support lower-income families in enrolling their children in preschool?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: The demands on our early childhood educators continue to be challenging.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can MSF provide an update on the number of preschool teachers recruited in the past three years?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Have we seen an increase, or has attrition outpaced recruitment?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: How does MSF intend to improve the working conditions of early childhood educators, step up recruitment and training of new educators, and reduce attrition?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: A quality early childhood sector must be underpinned by quality educators.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Many of these parents are from the lower-income groups, for whom shift work is more common.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Forward SG report said that childminding service options will be expanded.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Could the Minister share further updates on this programme, including how many families have benefited from it so far?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can MSF look into subsidising wages for childminders in order to attract more to join the scheme?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In order to scale up the service to benefit more parents, could MSF take the lead to roll out this programme nationwide?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: What are the current efforts in promoting this service to parents, and can it be integrated into KidSTART, ComLink and other related programmes for the low-income?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: We must do all we can to alleviate the anxieties and worries that couples face, when considering whether to have children.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: The availability of infant care has been a perennial issue for young couples.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can MSF provide an update on the current supply of infant care in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: How does MSF plan to grow affordable, safe, and reliable infant childminding services as a further option for young parents?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can MSF consider extending similar subsidies to those providing home-based infant care to bring the costs to parents comparable to out-of-pocket expense for infant care at Anchor Operators?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can we consider allowing parents to tap on the CDA to further defray cost?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Beyond affordability, we need to ensure the quality of home-based infant care.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Will MSF be mandating certain requirements for the childminders and operators, such as care ratio, mandatory training and background checks on childminders?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Will there be a requirement for home-based childminders to report incidents involving infants under their care?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Will MSF consider extending the HSS to include infant care so as to supplement supply?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: There is vast literature on the importance of early childhood education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The economic case for doing so is compelling; the reason is straightforward, as Nobel Prize-winning economist Jim Heckman explained.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Early childhood development entails building the necessary foundation for all subsequent human capital development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Without solid roots deeply planted, one's ability to absorb anything else that follows becomes compromised.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Hence, the returns to human capital investment tend to be highest during early childhood.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: These investments include engaged, supporting parents and teachers, learning cognitive and language skills, promoting social engagements and interactions, as well as improved health and nutrition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Many parents look forward to the day when they can finally send their kids to primary school, where fees drop to just $13 a month, compared to hundreds of dollars, especially in the earliest years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But to be clear, there are a slate of subsidies available which alter this calculus.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If you are a working mother, and if you earn a lower income, the total amount of subsidies available may be sufficient to fully offset fees.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If your child were to attend a typical childcare or kindergarten, there are also special dispensations for higher subsidy support, such as those under ComCare assistance, or if they are non-parent caregivers supporting the child, or if a parent becomes incarcerated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But there are still families who fall through the cracks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If a couple decides that the mother would not work, perhaps because they wish to spend more time on homemaking, or because the economics no longer works out when they have a sufficiently large number of children, then fees can quickly become burdensome.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The gap persists for those aged five to six, where enrolment rates are 95% to 93%, respectively.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Yet, it is this specific group, children from low-income households, that will benefit the most from early childhood interventions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That is why I believe that support for early childhood education should be made much more universal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This distinction, which may be motivated by a desire to ensure that mothers who are able to return to work do so, ends up inadvertently disadvantaging the child which, in turn, diminishes their future prospects for breaking out of poverty.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Another approach is to provide lower-income households with vouchers that can be applied to preschools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is not dissimilar to subsidies in practice but has one added advantage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It also sends a clear signal to underperforming preschools that they need to buck up or they will be relieved of Government financial support.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: During my Meet-the-People sessions, I often receive requests from parents to help in seeking infant care options nearest their homes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I am grateful to ECDA for their very prompt actions to help to match to vacancies as soon as possible.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: In cases where the young parents cannot wait, many of them share that they have resorted to informal childminding arrangements with family members or neighbours willing to help them in the caregiving.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: However, these informal arrangements do not qualify them for the same subsidies as formal infant care services do.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: How does MSF plan to pilot and scale such a programme to cover diverse family needs and geographical areas, ensuring that every family that needs such an arrangement can access the alternative infant care solutions?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Parents today are under tremendous stress as they juggle careers and providing quality care for their children and elderly parents, in some instances, trying to be good parents, sons and daughters.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, reliable, safe and affordable care services are imperative.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Specific to infant and childcare, abuse and ill-management cases reported in recent times are of great concern.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: These include the Kinderland cases last year, which was debated in this House; and another one, most recently involving a preschool at Seletar reported in the media just last week.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: These would have spooked many prospective parents and parents with young children.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, how is MSF going to continue to strengthen governance and at the same time, maintain quality, yet ensure costs are not passed on to parents excessively?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Preschool education is highly encouraged for all children as it can help them achieve important learning goals, such as building confidence, learning social skills and developing a good foundation in literacy and numeracy.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A trusted preschool can also allow mothers to return to the workplace with a peace of mind.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: SPARK certification was meant to raise the quality of preschools and it did help to ensure some standardisation and processes are in place.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Some early childhood educators find being uncertified more beneficial as they have greater flexibility to do more for the children.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Increasing salaries in the sector has not been enough to solve the high turnover problem.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The problem is no longer about remuneration but whether the work is realistically feasible for each person to shoulder.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Thirty years ago, Kindergarten 2 teachers could integrate Mother Tongue, English, art and music in creative manners to help children enjoy learning.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Each class had 42 children and the kids grew up fine.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Now, despite class sizes being cut to 25 kids, teachers still struggle because of the sheer amount of documentation they need to submit.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Lesson plans, curriculum, personal portfolio of each child, sometimes doubling up for the cooking or cleaning aunty if she is on medical leave.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Changing diapers or clothes for kids who soil their pants, pulling kids apart when they are fighting and giving more attention to children with special needs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: All these while making sure no child gets a scratch or a bruise, or bump their knees, which could then invite very anxious calls by parents for more accountability and more surveillance.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This will ensure that teachers' attention is on the children and not on completing paperwork meticulously.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I also suggest that we partner teachers, whose main job is to teach and nurture children, with a Child Development Specialist that specialises in the documentation and observation work.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Mr Chairman, as part of the Forward SG report, MSF put forth plans to uplift our lower-income families toward sustained progress by enhancing support through ComLink+ package, where families will be provided with dedicated family coaches, additional preschool subsidies, employment and home ownership support.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: In my Jalan Kayu (JK) Constituency, we started a JK Care Network to encourage companies and community partners in our neighbourhood to join hands in broadening support for our ComLink families.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: However, some partners have given feedback that there is a need for continuous and one-to-one family coaching to help some parents in ComLink families to better understand opportunities and priorities that can give their younger generation a better future.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: As such, I support the enhancements to provide closer family coaching in ComLink+ to facilitate ComLink families' decision-making and prioritisation of choices, thereby providing more social mobility for their children.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Two, how frequently can we expect the family coaches to be interacting with the ComLink families?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Three, and lastly, what measures will be put in place to assess the effectiveness of family coaching within ComLink+ and how will the assessments help shape future enhancements to the programme?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I welcome moves to provide additional assistance and support and empower low-income households.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: One feature of ComLink+ is having family coaches and voluntary befrienders working directly with beneficiaries' families, providing custom support.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This is indeed a fundamental aspect in facilitating and empowering families towards achieving their goals.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: For households who are facing life challenges: mentorship, facilitation and, at times, handholding, are crucial.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Financial and other tangible forms of assistance will not be effective without this human aspect.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Nonetheless, there are and will be cases where low-income households turn to unlicensed moneylenders.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I suggest that MSF could also explore working together with organisations focused on debt counselling, such as Adullam Life Counselling.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I have made numerous calls for the adoption of the social protection framework developed by the International Labour Organization (ILO) and the introduction of an annual social protection report, which tracks the effectiveness and efficacy of our social policies meant to uplift society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As Mayor of Central, I am privileged to serve these families with some excellent ComLink SSOs and Family Service Centre officers, especially in the Jalan Besar and Ang Mo Kio towns.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: However, my first-hand experience with assisting challenged families reveals complexities beyond what is initially apparent.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For example, it is not always easy to secure a preferred location for a family of eight living in a 2-room flat.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Timely school attendance then becomes a struggle when a single bathroom must accommodate the entire family in the mornings.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For example, a sole breadwinner relying on cash-based, flexible employment as a platform worker will find difficulties in foregoing his job to pursue higher education for a better future job.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Chairman, poverty, inequality and social mobility are related but distinct concepts.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Poverty is about whether one has enough or not.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: To use an analogy of an escalator: whether one is above or below a certain rung on the escalator.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Inequality is about the spread: how far apart folks are at various levels on the escalator.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: For mobility, there are actually two concepts – absolute and relative.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Absolute mobility is about how much one progresses over time or how much better one does compared to his or her parents.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is about how much the escalator is moving people upwards.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Whereas relative mobility is about how a person does relative to his or her peers, compared against how his or her parents did relative to their peers.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is about how much folks swap positions on the escalator over time.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I believe we must keep relative mobility strong.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Keep our society fluid and avoid permanent strata.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Because this gives hope and this holds our society together.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Yet, relative mobility tends to slow as we continue succeeding as absolute mobility continues benefiting everyone.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Therefore, how do we keep relative mobility alive for those at the bottom, even as we keep absolute mobility going for all?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This will be our defining social challenge, more than poverty and inequality.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: We keep absolute mobility going, keep the escalator moving for all, with macroeconomic policies.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But to keep relative mobility alive for those at the bottom and keep possible that swapping of positions on the escalator, we will need to go well beyond economics.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: We will need to mitigate unequal opportunities at birth; indeed, before birth and through life, dealing with the hand that folks are dealt by life.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It will take all of us on the escalator to move others up the escalator.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And having coaches and volunteers journey with these families.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: To keep relative mobility alive, we need ComLink+ to work.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: To this end, how does MSF plan to develop the manpower needed and galvanise society to come forward and contribute?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: More of such hubs all around Singapore will certainly ease the access of such services for persons with disabilities and their caregivers and enable them to live and participate in the community more actively.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Nonetheless, as we expand and build on such infrastructure, we must also make continuous efforts to involve the community, be it corporate, community, or grassroots partners, in different ways to provide different opportunities.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: With more involvement of the community, more coordination will also be needed to optimise each partner's contribution.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: In this aspect, I would like to ask MSF the following two questions.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: One, how will you better coordinate and spread out corporate and community partners to ensure adequate resources across various parts of Singapore?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: And two, how can we be more intentional in attracting young corporate executives to be on the boards of social service agencies to inject new ideas and activism to solve dynamic social issues?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: Mr Chairman, it is encouraging that our society is increasingly engaged in support of the social service sector.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: We see this in the sharing of skills and also in the area philanthropic initiatives.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: We see this in individuals across all age groups, large businesses alongside the smaller and medium industries.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: We see this among faith-based groups, community organisations – everyone coming together.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: We have been engaging Singaporeans in caring for our community from school days with the hope this will continue through adult life.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: As we chart our new social compact, we need to encourage active engagement across all strata of our society.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: How can we best convey information on the areas with most immediate needs?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: It takes a whole-of-community effort for spreading positivity, for doing good, for doing well.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: It was a welcome move in 2023 to celebrate social service partners and to remind everyone the important role corporate partners and agencies play in Singapore's new social compact.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: As we celebrate the Year of Social Service Volunteers in 2024, we remind ourselves that individuals, you and I, together with our families, friends and loved ones, have much to offer to the rest of society.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: Can the Ministry update plans they have put in place to inspire and mobilise more individuals to step up, to lead and volunteer?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: How will the Ministry continue to further galvanise different parts of our society to contribute to a caring and involved social compact?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I asked for changes to address significant gaps in provisions for living, learning and working, to alter societal perceptions of PwDs, to improve the policy-making and service structure for better collaboration amongst PwDs, their families and disability agencies and the Government, and to include the voices of PwDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I am grateful that many of these calls have been heeded.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: For instance, updates on the Enabling Masterplan 2030, or EMP 2030, are accessible now on the MSF website though they require navigating through quite a few pages before one can find them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I call upon MSF to proactively push out this information so that affected stakeholders are assured of progress.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I also want to propose four areas for further improvement today.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: They should also link these outputs to outcomes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: This approach would then offer insights into the health conditions of PwDs, for example, their readiness when they leave formal schooling, caregiver confidence in obtaining information and assistance, and the level of public awareness and acceptance of PwDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Although challenging to connect outputs to outcomes and, like Mr Xie Yao Quan said, to have even impact, I think that is even more difficult, it is crucial for the EMP 2030 implementation team to begin this analysis to support further informed contributions by other stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: With rapid changes in society and technology, the eight-year EMP 2030 will become obsolete, outdated; not totally, but quite a bit will be outdated.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: On inclusive insurance, I am deeply appreciative of the strong support from the Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Life Insurance Association.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: They have collaborated with charities such as the Autism Resource Centre to develop a guide to raise awareness of disabilities and enhance transparency of insurance risk assessment approach towards health insurance undertaking.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: There are still significant challenges that need further study.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: For example, insurance companies often hesitate to cover individuals with disabilities who disclose their medication use, failing to recognise that those who follow their prescribed medication regimens are likely to maintain or improve their health status.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: On criminal justice, I repeat my call for a review by MSF and the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) of the appropriate adult scheme to enhance police investigations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: There is also a pressing need to explore a facility or programme ensuring that persons with disabilities who are incarcerated are placed in appropriate physical facilities and suitable rehab programmes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: For my last point today, on funding models for essential services.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I seek MSF's considered and favourable responses to the four points I made.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Chairman, it is encouraging to know that the Government is continuing to make significant efforts to promote inclusive employment, including the upcoming Workplace Fairness Legislation (WFL) to promote more employment opportunities for PwDs and the Enhanced Enabling Employment Credit (EEC) to increase the support level employers will get when hiring PwDs.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: All these efforts are important and steps in the right direction to meet our inclusive employment goals as a fair and inclusive nation.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Notwithstanding these commendable efforts, with the changing nature of work, it is also important to track more granular employment data so that we are aware of the effectiveness of various strategies and areas to expand resources in to keep the relevance and sustainability of PwD's employment.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Lastly, whether the income level of the PwDs will enable them to sustain independent living till retirement age like the rest of the workforce, especially when their parents are ageing and finding more difficulties in caring for them?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Ong Hua Han, you can take your three cuts together.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, while the Government has through Budget 2024 underscored its commitment to expand sheltered workshop spaces going forward, I would like to stress that we need to focus on empowering as many PwDs as possible to take up open employment roles.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, the success of the Sheltered Workshop to Work Programme is critical.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: And three, could MSF also share what is being done to equip PwDs with the skills and support necessary to transition into open employment settings?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Last Friday, Minister Chan said that he wanted special education (SPED) students to have pathways integrated with their post-18 work, life and care arrangements.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: While we look out for PwDs in the post-18 space, we must also remember that their parents continue to play a vital role in their well-being and care.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Some PwDs depend on parental support in their adult years.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Others need parental support while transitioning into independent living, and the rest need support on a long-term basis.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I know – and a few of us in this House know, this intimately, too – parents who give up their career or make significant sacrifices to look after their children with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: They are growing older, and their own medical expenses are also rising.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: They continue to support their children with disabilities every day.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: They incur additional expenses on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: There is no break from caregiving for many parents.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, I urge MSF to put in place robust support mechanisms to ease both their financial and emotional burden.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: By doing so, we can empower parents to continue providing care while safeguarding their own health and well-being.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, on means testing, I raise two key suggestions today.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: One, that the income threshold of means-tested schemes should be recalibrated to at least align with current median household per capita income figures; and two, that our means testing framework should be improved to take into account actual costs borne by families with PwDs.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: These are points I had raised before in my maiden speech in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I am concerned about the accessibility of existing support schemes, such as the Assistive Technology Fund (ATF), Enabling Transport Subsidy (ETS), or the Disabled Person Scheme (DPS).

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Access to the ATF remains limited due to stringent eligibility criteria based on household income.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: To qualify, gross monthly per capita household income (PCHI) must strictly fall below $2,000.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, access to the ETS is not available if gross monthly PCHI exceeds $2,800 for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: As for the DPS, if the combined income of a four-member household exceeds $6,500, that works out to a PCHI of $1,625, the PwD cannot benefit from the scheme.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: This is despite them being certified as permanently disabled and incapable of taking public transport.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Could this be because access to the scheme is too limited?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: According to SingStat, median monthly PCHI from work has risen to almost $3,300 in 2022.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, the three schemes I have just listed all have means-tested income criteria inconsistent with each other and also fall below median income levels.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: To the end-user people in need of these schemes, it is difficult to understand why this is so.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, it does not look like we are short on policies or support schemes.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: What we need to do is to recalibrate our means-testing criteria.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: If we can improve our existing support mechanisms, we will already do a lot to ensure that our policies effectively serve those in need.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It has been doing very good work in plugging a gap in the local disability services landscape.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We owe the board members of SNTC, past and present, a debt of gratitude.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Government, particularly MSF, has played a crucial role in making trust services accessible by providing between 90% to 100% subsidies for the costs involved in the set-up, pre-activation, activation and post-activation of the trust accounts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Without the Government absorbing the costs, I believe the take-up rate amongst Singaporeans, particularly our lower-income families, would be much lower.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As at 2022, 65% of trusts created were by families in Housing and Development Board flats.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It is clear however that more Singaporean households can benefit from subscribing to such services.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Our rapidly ageing population and shrinking household sizes contribute two drivers to the thinning of caregiver support within families with persons with special needs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: First, I wish to ask what steps can be taken to increase the take-up rate of trust services amongst eligible families, especially amongst low-income families.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In this context, I wish to suggest that MSF agencies, social service and grassroots organisations work together to proactively identify families that can benefit so that SNTC can educate them on the benefits of trust services.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Next, I note that SNTC evolved to provide, not just trust services, but other offerings such as subsidised insurance term plans.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: So, my second question is, what other plans does SNTC have to ensure the financial security of such persons?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Families with children with development needs require additional support and resources to help them manage.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How is the Government helping the parents of these children?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While every child is different, there are general principles and broad strategies which parents can learn and adopt for their own use at home.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, courses and training can be helpful, all the more so for parents of children with development needs.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry share with House what training and advisories are provided to this group of parents?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Individuals with special needs and their families, see SG Enable as a one-stop centre, where they can seek support and resources to address the issues they may face.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is very heartening to see these endeavours.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The needs of the special needs community are, however, very diverse.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Understandably, it would be challenging to fulfil and address all requests and issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I can imagine there are various situations that come to the attention of SG Enable including requests for financial support for assistive devices, requests for placements in SPED schools or programmes, or requests for support with caregiving arrangements.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe it would be imperative to understand the gaps to be able to further enhance its services.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: SG Enable has also been working with many different partners to come up with a myriad of services.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: What more can be done to strengthen these relationships to be able to support the work done by the agency?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I heard with interest when Member Ms Denise Phua spoke about fostering a more robust ecosystem of partnership in her speech during the Budget debate a few weeks ago.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This is very much in line with the spirit of Budget 2024, to build our shared future together.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: She shared about a grounds-up effort in her Kampung Glam division known as Purple Hearts, a special needs family network, where volunteers reach out to the families and seek to match the needs with resources in different agencies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I will certainly take up the offer to learn from her and see how I can replicate this in Bukit Batok East.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In Bukit Batok East, we have our BBE Inclusive Family Day, where we bring together different agencies and partners to showcase their services and support to the special needs community and use that platform to edify the larger community about our friends who are differently abled.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe strongly that it is important to nurture partnerships and understanding within our local communities in the heartlands.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We should create more opportunities to build these ground networks as part of SG Enable's larger vision to support inclusiveness.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In Member Denise Phua's speech, she also made a strong call for the Government to take a better lead in bringing partners together to amongst other things, understand the gaps in the landscape and facilitate more meaningful allocation of resources and effective contribution.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Beyond income, work raises confidence, self-esteem, provides identity, structure and purpose to one's life.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: It can also provide persons with special needs with a community of support at the workplace.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Persons with special needs are physically and neurologically diverse.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: They are not a monolithic group of helpless or disabled care recipients.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The framing of persons with special needs labels them as needy.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The framing of neurodiversity as a problem labels people who have them as problematic.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Instead of being fixated on their limitations, we can shift our lenses to focus instead on their unique strengths.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: They are examples of successful employers who have observed their productivity to be often higher than normal employees.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We need to adopt a strength-based approach by seeing divergence as an asset and not a problem.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The culture of acceptance and awareness from co-workers, as well as the parents' or caregivers' mindsets, is essential for employment to be successful and sustained.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We need to change the mindset of the whole of society and not just employers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We can just as easily see persons with special needs as specially able or specially gifted if we start focusing on their strengths.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: People in wheelchairs are hired as security guards as they have better visibility at pocket height and are also able to move faster on a chase than people on foot.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: We can improve public awareness of what neurodiversity is and start to recognise the supernormal attributes that specially abled persons have if we only saw them as such.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: For example, autism, currently classified as a disability, is also known as a neurodiverse condition, amongst others such as obsessive compulsive disorder, dyslexia and ADHD.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: What great leaps might we make in the future if we started to approach and excavate the special gifts of these children?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: If we adopt the approach much like Professor X in the Marvel series to nurture them, such as the X-Men, and hone their special abilities for good, it is the limitation of society's imagination and resourcefulness that renders them as disabled.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I urge MSF to set a goal to leapfrog employment success by shifting this lens of special needs to specially abled for our friends in this community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As a country, we have been able to weather storms and emerge stronger because we have strong families and a strong social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Forward SG reaffirmed that Singaporeans continue to value the importance of the family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There was also strong consensus to be a society where all families have the opportunity to succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will touch on three key approaches to achieve this mission.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, working together to support families through every stage of life, strengthening marriages, supporting parents from their children's early years and caring for our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, we will move beyond assistance to empowering families in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have started this through ComLink+ and will go further to uplift children from lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, the Government will come alongside the social service sector, corporates and Singaporeans to strengthen families, uplift those in need and reinforce their efforts to ensure sustained impact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We invite more to volunteer and contribute their time, their talent and their treasures.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, we will build a caring and inclusive society and sustain social mobility in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, couples are staying together longer and recent cohorts show a lower proportion of marriages dissolving before the 10th anniversary.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am heartened that more couples recognise the importance of continuing to invest in their marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They proactively look for marriage and parenting resources rather than seeking help only when the relationship is on the rocks.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We affirm society's commitment to families and will continue to strengthen families, our anchor in years to come.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We do this by supporting families throughout their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As I shared in the Ministry of Health (MOH) Committee of Supply, we are enhancing support for couples in their journey through pregnancy and parenthood.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The early years of our children are critical and for new parents, possibly the most challenging time too.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the years, parents have greater access to affordable and quality preschools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are also helping working parents balance work responsibilities and infant caregiving.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government is tackling this in several ways, which Minister of State Sun Xueling will elaborate on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We encourage eligible fathers to use the paternity leave and work is in progress to allow more fathers to benefit from the additional two weeks of leave.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we do not stop at the early years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are making programmes and resources even more accessible to support the range of family relationships.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Families for Life (FFL) movement, led by the FFL Council, brings together various partners to offer marriage and parenting programmes in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have also recently partnered Anchor Operators to offer FFL parenting programmes to parents of preschoolers in their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Ng Ling Ling referred to the collective effort by everyone in society to build a Singapore Made for Families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: That is why the Council is also looking to work with employers, who play a crucial role in fostering a family-friendly environment, to offer marriage and parenting resources or talks at their workplaces.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Community partners and volunteers are equally critical in supporting our mission to build strong families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is wonderful to see the FFL movement growing steadily.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last year, over 150 corporate and community partners, such as CapitaLand Malls and Singapore Heart Foundation, alongside 400 volunteers, came together to support the National Family Week.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We look forward, too, to collaborating with more partners to offer families an engaging experience.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With the effort of many, we build a Singapore Made for Families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked how we can foster a society where no one is left behind.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our goal is for every Singaporean family to be a strong and stable family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Lower-income families often face additional challenges, as Ms Denise Phua observed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, families may have to stretch their limited finances to meet different needs while also balancing their work, caregiving and rest.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This can lead to "bandwidth tax", where families are focused on the day-to-day and not be able to plan for the long-term.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond providing social assistance, we want to partner families as they work towards their aspirations and reinforce their strengths to build better lives for themselves and their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In other words, we want to move beyond assistance to empowerment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: That is why we introduced ComLink+ as part of Forward SG.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ComLink+ families now have a dedicated family coach who coaches, motivates and journeys with them as they work towards their longer-term goals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes families supported by Family Service Centres (FSCs), whose case workers perform the family coach function.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As families take active steps towards their goals, they can receive financial top-ups from ComLink+ Progress Packages to multiply the impact of their efforts and help them better focus on achieving their goals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These enhancements to ComLink+ and partnerships with FSCs show how we place family-centricity at the heart of everything we do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As Mr Melvin Yong observed, besides lower-income families, FSCs also serve other families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Like general practitioner (GP) clinics providing healthcare in the community, FSCs are community-based agencies that provide casework expertise to support families with social and emotional needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For over 30 years, FSCs have evolved their practice to serve changing needs of clients to help them achieve the "3S"s – Self-reliance, Stability and Social mobility.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, the landscape of family services has grown and FSCs work alongside many other agencies to support families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A family with complex needs, apart from receiving support from an FSC, may also receive support from other social service agencies (SSAs) for domestic violence, family counselling or youth programmes for their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While SSAs put in effort to coordinate with one another, the family may still find it tedious to interface with multiple partners.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Another concern is that we may not always be addressing the underlying issues, as each partner is focused on tackling the issue at hand.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the next decade, we will also face more demographic challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will become a super-aged society and household structures may change.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But as our society changes, there are opportunities for us to adapt to meet the emerging needs and support families in an even more coordinated manner.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In line with the spirit of Forward SG, we will engage and co-create the future landscape with the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, we have been concerted in our efforts to support lower-income families towards achieving social mobility.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A key aspect of our strategy to sustain social mobility in Singapore is to uplift children and for all children to have a good start in life regardless of their background.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While preschool enrolment rates of children from lower-income families have increased, these remain lower than the national average.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: About eight in 10 children aged three to four from lower-income families are enrolled in preschool, compared to the national average of nine in 10.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This could be due to a variety of factors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Parents may have concerns about being able to afford preschool fees, be less aware of the benefits of preschool, or may have to juggle work and family commitments with fewer resources.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will be rolling out several measures to help children from lower-income families reap the benefits of our investments in the early years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, we will provide greater assurance to lower-income families that they can afford to send their children to preschool.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: All families on ComCare assistance or residing in public rental flats already automatically qualify for maximum childcare subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced in the Budget speech, we will extend similar support to more lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, we will expand proactive outreach to all lower-income families from the third quarter of 2024 to encourage them to enrol their children in preschools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Preschool outreach workers and ComLink+ family coaches will work with parents to help them understand the importance of preschool and to enrol their child in a suitable preschool.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As part of the ComLink+ Packages, ComLink+ families can benefit from financial top-ups when they enrol their children early and send them to preschool regularly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, we will support families in maximising the benefits of quality preschool education.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We recognise that children from lower-income families may require more support even after they enrol in preschools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Their families may also have less resources to support their learning at home.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: From the second quarter of this year, we will provide more resources to selected Anchor Operator preschools to equip them in providing effective and timely support to the children under their care.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Anchor Operators will co-fund this targeted support and use the additional resources to support the children, such as providing dedicated small group learning lessons and addressing the challenges that families face in sending their children to preschool regularly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As Minister Maliki shared, MOE will also similarly strengthen initiatives in MOE Kindergartens to support children from lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Taken together, these measures will help address the challenges that lower-income families face and enable their children to learn, play and develop holistically alongside their peers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In partnership with the FFL Council, we will increase the accessibility of parenting resources for lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In this way, the efforts of parents and preschool educators complement each other and lay a strong foundation for the children to flourish.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our efforts to strengthen families are made possible by a strong social service ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This comprises a group of deeply committed partners, professionals and volunteers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The different groups of partners, our SSAs, academics and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) and corporates, come together to support those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Keith Chua asked about our plans to attract, recruit and retain professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government and partners, including SSAs, must work together to make the social service sector a career of choice.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One key aspect is to ensure that the salaries in the sector are commensurate with the hard work and skillsets of our professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MSF and National Council of Social Service (NCSS) also adjusted funding to ensure professionals supporting our funded programmes can be paid within the guidelines.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We expect our funded providers to adhere to and pay employees within the guidelines over the next three years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will work closely with SSAs that require additional support, including providing targeted consultancy support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The social service sector is a people-oriented sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: All the more, we need to care for our people, so that they can better care for our beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Apart from a range of NCSS' resources on self-care and wellness that our professionals can access, the SkillsFuture Tripartite Taskforce also promotes emotional and mental wellness at work through the Joy@Social Services movement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MSF and NCSS will continue creating pathways for more to enter the sector and progress in their career.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, we are working with IHLs to engage students.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are also attracting mid-career entrants through the Career Conversion Programmes and these professionals can benefit from the new SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme announced by Deputy Prime Minister Wong in the Budget Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together with SSAs, we are improving the value proposition of roles through job redesign, strengthening their organisational capabilities and working on talent retention measures.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To support the development of our professionals, we have the Skills Framework for Social Service.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are also working with relevant professional associations and providers to monitor the standards, qualification and training required for the different professions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, we will build a stronger social service sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our ecosystem is made of another important group of people: our volunteers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Volunteers are people who give generously their time, talent and treasures to support others.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We see these in the individuals that make up our MSFCare Network.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They work with MSF in initiatives, such as ComLink+.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Since October 2022, she has been befriending Mdm Marlina and her son.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And as any parent would know, the transition into primary school is an exciting but hectic one.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When Mdm Marlina had difficulty buying school materials needed for her son at Primary 1 due to her financial situation, Susan guided them through the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme application.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Her son managed to start primary school with all his books and school uniform needed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, Susan continues offering the family a listening ear and assisting them in meeting their needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, Susan and the family coach explained the importance of getting Mdm Marlina's son glasses as soon as possible when he was found to need them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Susan found community support to make the glasses more affordable and later accompanied them to make a pair.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We thank volunteers like Susan for their dedication and partnership.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, our volunteers give generously, by contributing their talent and skills.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, employees of SP Group regularly volunteer with SSAs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Some are seasoned volunteers who are familiar with the challenges faced by vulnerable families, so they contribute their insights and co-curate programmes with SSAs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Others tap on their own areas of expertise to contribute.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Tay Xin Ci and her engineer colleagues run classes to teach children from vulnerable families how to build solar powered toy cars.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The children learn not only about solar power but are inspired by these "big brothers and sisters".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Xin Ci is also part of the SP Heart Workers committee, which spearheads volunteering activities for SP Group throughout the year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When individuals with different skills come forward, families benefit from the opportunities and range of support offered.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They contribute their resources and give in different ways.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One way is through donations to the Community Chest, or ComChest, which go towards supporting services for vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will talk about two ComChest initiatives – SHARE and Change for Charity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: SHARE reminds us that sustained giving, even in small amounts, can add up and lead to meaningful impact over time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many donors put in a few dollars to SHARE each month.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through SHARE, we also see how acts of caring often start from young.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This year is the 40th Anniversary of our iconic mascot, Sharity, who will continue engaging students in schools to inculcate the values of caring and sharing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Gerald Rodrigues is part of the pioneer batch of donors on SHARE and a former Police officer.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: His interactions with lower-income families ignited a desire to help those with less, as he empathised with the hardships they faced.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And he continues to donate regularly through SHARE.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Donors like Gerald inspire us to care for others.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More recently, we introduced Change for Charity to amplify giving through a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: City Developments Limited (CDL) is one of the businesses that has implemented Change for Charity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At Millennium Hotels and Resorts, a subsidiary group of CDL with six hotels in Singapore, they make it convenient for customers to donate.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Andy Tan led his team in brainstorming ideas to weave giving mechanisms in their business model and pushing for the implementation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They place donation boxes at the check-in counters and food and beverage (F&B) outlets, to make giving more accessible to their customers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Customers can also donate when they are paying their bills or by redeeming membership reward points.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With the customers' spending and contributions as the starting point, the amount is multiplied as the hotel donates a dollar for every dinner buffet cover.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through this, we hope to create a multiplier effect that amplifies giving in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
