text: Mr Chairman, we are strengthening touchpoints with Singaporeans at every stage of their lives to encourage them to contribute to the society – their time, talent, their treasure.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To the questions raised by Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Mr Keith Chua and Ms Ng Ling Ling – this is how we will galvanise the community, from young to old, from one generation to the next.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue to work with our partners, from corporates to SSAs, to rally more to contribute.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Corporates have shown growing interest in being more strategic in their corporate social responsibility effort.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are making progress in developing the Sustainable Philanthropy Framework to guide them in benchmarking and articulating their social impact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS has been engaging leaders across diverse sectors to better shape the framework.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This month, we will be extending our reach by holding consultations with the wider business community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are also enhancing the capabilities of volunteer managers in SSAs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Volunteer managers can access resources from the NCSS Volunteer Resource Hub to guide them in tapping the creativity and expertise of volunteers to address social issues and to better attract and retain them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, we create opportunities for more to give and build a society that cares for one another.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay. :   Chairman, families are the foundation of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government will continue strengthening our support to enable families to grow and thrive through every stage of life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In line with Forward SG plans, the Government will strengthen support for lower-income families by focusing on social empowerment through the ComLink+.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Volunteers play a pivotal role in uplifting families in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, under Project DIAN@M³, volunteers have assisted 250 Malay ComLink+ families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These volunteers also check in with them regularly and address immediate concerns by connecting them to available support schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Moving forward, volunteers will continue to work closely with ComLink+ officers to provide more comprehensive support for ComLink+ families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am confident that with the help of volunteers, we will work towards helping these families to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility. : Chairperson, carrying forth the spirit of Forward SG, let us work together to build a caring and inclusive society, a brighter and better Singapore for all families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their views.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is committed to providing every child with a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Preschools play an important role in supporting our children's development while meeting parents' caregiving needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is an important part of our vision in realising a Singapore Made for Families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked how we will make preschools accessible and affordable for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government provides funding to Anchor and Partner Operators to ensure that they keep within fee caps, while investing in quality improvements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government also provides all parents with basic subsidies, as well as additional subsidies for eligible families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This comprehensive approach to preschool affordability, where we keep fees charged for Government-supported preschools low and provide childcare subsidies to parents, is more effective than giving vouchers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will further enhance preschool affordability in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will make a final reduction in 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked how we will continue to attract and retain early childhood educators to support the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The well-being of our educators is important to us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our educators dedicate themselves to the nurturing of our children and play a critical role in driving the quality of care and education for our young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA has been enhancing the career proposition of early childhood educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We announced the Continuing Professional Development Roadmap in 2021 and the Leadership Development Framework as well as salary improvements in 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to monitor and review to ensure educators' salaries remain competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also improving the working conditions and well-being of educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: From 2024, similar to Primary Schools, Teacher's Day and Children's Day will be designated as preschool holidays.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The existing six days of preschool closure have also been repositioned as "Development Days" to give educators dedicated time to focus on their individual and team development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: From 2025, childcare centres are no longer required to operate on Saturdays.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With this, preschool teachers will have an additional half-day of rest every week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To attract more Singaporeans to the sector, ECDA is relaunching the "Shape Our Tomorrow" campaign in 2024 to strengthen the public's understanding of the early childhood (EC) sector and recognise EC educators as a respected profession.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Carrie Tan also suggested the SPARK certification process be reviewed to reduce educators' workload.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SPARK is an accreditation framework to guide preschools in raising their quality, such as in the areas of teaching and learning and administration and management of centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The number of SPARK-certified preschools has been growing over the years and stands at 1,000 preschools or 58% of the sector today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA is reviewing SPARK and plans to roll out the refreshed SPARK certification in 2025 to set the next bound of quality for our preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To reduce workload on educators, we are exploring various ways to keep the work required for SPARK certification manageable, such as streamlining requirements and tapping on technology to reduce the documentation and administraton work involved.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling touched on child safety in preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Preschools must be a safe and nurturing environment for our children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA ensures that our educators have the necessary qualifications and skills to effectively and safely care for and educate children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Besides basic screening requirements and health declarations, all educators must meet the academic, professional and language requirements before they can be certified by ECDA and deployed in our preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As part of these requirements, educators must undergo training programmes where they learn classroom management strategies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA also regularly updates the training curriculum of the teachers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have recently made it clearer with more specific examples on what constitutes inappropriate behaviour to guide our educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are also regular sector-wide briefings and circulars to update educators on the latest research and teaching pedagogies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where there is negligence from operators, ECDA will take them to task with regulatory fines and levers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where individual teachers have committed offences, they will be charged by the Police and punished under the Children and Young Persons Act and/or the Penal Code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA's powers are enforced through the Early Childhood Development Centres Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are working on this right now even as I speak.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We give our assurance to parents that where there is evidence that operators and/or educators have been errant, ECDA and the Police will commence investigations immediately, suspend educators who are in a position to harm children and take them to justice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents who suspect that their child has been subjected to child mismanagement should report to ECDA and the Police, so that investigations can be swiftly carried out, investigations are not compromised and due process can be taken.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: During the Forward SG engagements, we also have heard many Singaporeans share their love and aspirations for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the same time, some have also shared about the struggles and anxieties that they faced in raising their children – especially from parents of infants and parents of children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many parents explained that the most challenging period was during the first 18 months, as parents are adapting to a new phase of life to care for an infant while juggling work responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As mentioned by Minister Masagos, for children aged three and above, preschools can be the best option to meet parents' caregiving needs while supporting the child's holistic development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For children below three years, what is important is for them to build nurturing relationships with significant caregivers and for caregivers to be responsive towards their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, most Singaporean parents prefer to play this role and care for infants themselves or rely on the help of family members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Ng Ling Ling have asked how we can better support parents in caring for their infants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As mentioned in the Forward SG report, the Government will consider how paid parental leave can be further increased.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, around one in five infants are enrolled in infant care centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to ramp up centre-based infant care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will be yet another caregiving option for parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Childminders, some of us may know them as "nannies" are not a new concept.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They were more common in Singapore in the 1970s and 1980s.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some childminders look after a few children in their own homes while others travel to a family's home to look after the child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They are less common today, as parents may be unsure of where to look for trusted childminders or they may find childminding relatively more expensive as compared to other caregiving options, such as infant care centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last year, in a work visit to Denmark, France and the UK, I learnt that these countries have put in place requirements, such as background checks on the childminders and financial support to parents, such as subsidies, to make childminding more accessible to parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents can then have greater flexibility to choose what is best for them in terms of their caregiving needs and preferences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, parents may prefer a more structured setting during working hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They may then opt for infant care centres for their infants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Those who prefer more flexible hours or more individualised care in a home-setting may for opt for infant childminding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will thus launch a pilot and appoint childminding operators and work with them to expand infant childminding services in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Community spaces, such as community centres, will be in areas of high infant care demand so that parents can conveniently access childminding services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents also have more flexibility to discuss their care preferences and requirements with the childminder.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also extend the usage of CDA to further defray the cost of childminding under the pilot.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We understand that the safety is a key consideration for parents when deciding the care arrangements for their infants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To give parents more assurance under this pilot, ECDA will conduct background checks on operators and childminders and require operators to meet certain service requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These service requirements include: (a) assessing the suitability and homes of the childminders; (b) putting in place guidelines for child-safe practices and responsibilities of childminders; (c) disclosing childminders' profile to parents; (d) establishing processes for incident management; and (e) ensuring that childminders undergo required training in areas, such as basic infant care, first aid training and food safety and hygiene.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA will also work with operators to co-develop industry standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes laying out what constitutes a safe childminding environment and the respective responsibilities of operators and childminders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will ensure baseline service standards across the appointed operators and help to uplift the childminding sector in general.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The pilot will allow us to assess the receptiveness of parents to infant childminding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As this is a new pilot, we have engaged parents, childminders and childminding operators to hear their views to help us refine the parameters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue such engagements and announce more details in the second-half of 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked how we will support parents of children with developmental needs to help their child reach their full potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Children with developmental challenges have diverse and unique needs and require different types of support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some can be supported in their preschools, while others may require more specialised interventions at centres providing Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: International studies have also shown that parents are in the best position to embed intervention related to social and emotional skills in their children's daily lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: During the six-month programme, caregivers will learn from professionals through group workshops and individual coaching sessions on how to support their child's development at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA plans to launch the EIPIC-Care pilot in the second half of 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For children who require more support, we have been increasing the number of Government-funded places for children requiring medium to high levels of early intervention support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will help to reduce overall wait times for enrolment into an early intervention centre so that children with developmental needs can receive timely support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To provide stronger financial support for families of older children with special needs, Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced in his Budget speech that we will make Special Education (SPED) Schools and Special Student Care Centres (SSCC) more affordable for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will reduce the fees paid to bring the proportion of household income paid for out-of-pocket expenses closer to that of their typically developing peers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Hazel Poa asked on the use of restorative justice in cases of spousal violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As families navigate various milestones in their life journey, we want to build strong families and ensure parents are equipped to build safe havens for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Unfortunately, some families are not safe when violence happens at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To strengthen protection for survivors of violence, we moved the Family Violence (Amendment) Bill in Parliament last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These provisions also strengthen powers for the Government to rehabilitate perpetrators, which is crucial to helping families reconcile once protection and safety for survivors have been achieved.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our social service practitioners also support families at risk of harm or who are experiencing violence to address the root causes for the use of violence and work with the survivor and perpetrator to heal and restore relationships where possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Family members, including children, may attend these counselling sessions to achieve healing and restoration of family relationships where it is safe to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, we will not hesitate to take firm measures when such restoration is not possible in the immediate term.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes exercising the full powers of the law to take the perpetrators to task and to ensure the safety and protection of the survivors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Families are the bedrock of our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to give parents and parents-to-be greater assurance in the caregiving of their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to provide every child with a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is an important part of our vision in realising a Singapore Made For Families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to make preschools more accessible and affordable for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will further reduce childcare fee caps at Anchor and Partner Operators by $40 in 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will make a final reduction in 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also increase the number of Government-supported preschool places, so that 80% of preschoolers can have a place in a Government-supported preschool by 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to maintain this 80% from 2025 to 2030.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also heard from parents that the most challenging period was during their child's infancy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To better support parents in the care of infants, the Government will work with service providers to launch an infant childminding service to provide another caregiving option for parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will provide funding to keep the childminding service affordable for parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA will also work with operators to co-develop industry standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes laying out what constitutes a safe childminding environment and the respective responsibilities of operators and childminders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents of children with development needs also require greater support to help their child reach their full potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have seen many volunteers who have worked alongside professionals to support our families in need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Marsha Hernatasha and Ms Qistina Mohamed Nasir are friends who are volunteers together for KidSTART Garden Wonders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As volunteers, they welcome KidSTART families, pack and distribute goody bags and engage the children during the storytelling sessions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Marsha and Ms Qistina sees volunteering as an opportunity to do something good and give back to families with young children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chairman, talking to Singaporeans from all walks of life, one topic that often comes up is, "What would Singapore in the future look like?" Will we be a more caring and inclusive society?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Can Singapore be a place made for all families, one where lower-income families have a fair chance to achieve their aspirations, and one where persons with disabilities can fulfil their true potential?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF is working hard with families and communities to make these statements a reality.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I recently met Ms Aini and Mr Wali, a young couple who welcomed their first child Laila in 2022.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They are currently living in a public rental flat and they hope to purchase their first BTO flat soon.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Aini is looking to return to a cabin crew job, while Wali is striving to turn his passion for stand-up paddling into a full-time business.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The couple is working hard to realise their dreams: to achieve their career goals, buy a home and provide a good future for young Laila.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But they are unsure how they can get there.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is where MSF's ComLink+ family coaches, like Mr Zeke, come in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our family coaches journey with ComLink+ families and support their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The family coach considers the family's unique circumstances, needs and strengths and co-develops an action plan with the family to help the family achieve its goals, one step at a time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through discussions with Zeke, Aini and Wali agreed that an important and immediate goal for the family was to secure stable employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This would enable them to repay their loans and save for their BTO flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With Aini on board with the action plan, Zeke then connected her with a career coach at Workforce Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Zeke also provided helpful perspectives and suggestions on balancing work with parenting responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: After some consideration, Aini and Wali decided that Wali could take care of Laila when Aini needs to fly for work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With care arrangements sorted out, she can now look for a cabin crew job with peace of mind.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As the family coach, Zeke is providing Aini and Wali with the sort of structured approach Ms Ng Ling Ling talked about, to achieve stability and make better decisions for the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The nationwide rollout of ComLink started in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And we are now ready to proceed with ComLink+.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan would also be pleased to know that with ComLink+, we will have integrated support across multiple programmes, including KidSTART, UPLIFT Community Network and Project Dian@M3.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to strengthen the leadership role of the family coach to coordinate support across programmes and services, so that ComLink+ families can enjoy comprehensive, coordinated and convenient support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: All in, each family coach, aided by volunteer befrienders, is expected to support between 25 and 35 families and meet with them at least one to two times a month at the beginning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In a shift from social assistance to empowerment, we will provide financial top-ups through ComLink+ Progress Packages to recognise and supplement ComLink+ families' efforts in working towards stable employment, financial stability, home ownership and giving their children a good start in education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The first ComLink+ Package for Preschool will be launched in the second half of this year and we will roll out the rest of the ComLink+ Packages subsequently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The early years are crucial for a child's learning and development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Enrolling in preschool by age three and attending preschool regularly will give Laila a good start in life and better prepare her for Primary 1.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This includes a one-time CDA top-up of $500 when the child is enrolled in preschool in the year that he or she turns three, and $200 for each quarter that the child achieves at least 75% attendance in the preschool.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These top-ups are funded by one of our ComLink+ anchor partners, DBS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: All they need to do is to enrol and send their child to preschool regularly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Laila continues her preschool education, Aini will also benefit from the preschool subsidies given to lower-income households.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Gerald Giam will be pleased to know that full-day childcare fees for children from all lower-income families at Anchor Operator preschools cost as low as $3 monthly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: If Laila regularly attends a Government-supported preschool until six, not only will the ComLink+ CDA top-ups fully pay for her preschool fees, there will also be ample balance remaining in her CDA that can be used for her healthcare and other primary school expenses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since the nationwide scale-up of ComLink, we have been encouraged by the good response from the families, many of whom have agreed to work with us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And we are now ready to embark on our next move: to provide ComLink+ support to families beyond those in public rental housing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These families face similar challenges as our ComLink+ families and would also benefit from family coach support and the ComLink+ Progress Packages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: ComLink+ embodies our refreshed approach to support our lower-income families, something Mr Melvin Yong touched upon.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our family coaches recognise each family's unique aspirations, strengths and circumstances and work with them to chart their next steps.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They also take the lead to coordinate and integrate support for the families they serve, giving families more headspace to plan for their own future and achieve their goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, our shift from social assistance to social empowerment, where we help families move forward as they work towards a better future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: ComLink+ aims to empower families to achieve the "3S"s outcomes of stability, self-reliance and, eventually, social mobility over the long term.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is distinct from social assistance that serves immediate needs but may have less direct and sustained impact on longer-term outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, our greatest support comes from partnerships: our volunteers and our partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our ComLink+ partners across the people, private and public sectors contribute what they can to support others in need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our anchor partners, DBS, Singapore Pools and, most recently, The Ngee Ann Kongsi, fund some of the ComLink+ Progress Packages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many DBS staff have also stepped forward as Befrienders, while Singapore Pools staff are also volunteering at various ComLink+ programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Students like Ansel Lim and Adele Koo from NUS, whom I have also met recently, are Aini's Befrienders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They play with Laila and organise outings with the families and in this Year of Celebrating Volunteers, I want to express my heartfelt thanks to our ComLink+ volunteers for devoting your time and energy to journey alongside these families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We welcome community partners to work alongside ComLink+ to offer complementary programmes where there is a need, such as debt counselling, financial literacy, homework supervision and sports programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In this way, everyone contributes to uplifting our lower-income families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Looking ahead, we hope that ComLink+ will support families' pursuit of long-term aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Going forward, we will track ComLink+ families' progress towards the "3S"s outcomes and work with local academics to evaluate the efficacy of the ComLink+ Progress Packages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In every society, there will be those who struggle from time to time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, what really reflects our moral fibre as a society is how we work together to make sure that no one is permanently stranded at the bottom of the barrel.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As our lower-income families work hard to build a better tomorrow for themselves, let us support and journey alongside them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I now move on to enabling persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SG Enable plays a key role in galvanising an extensive range of partners towards our EMP 2030 goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Members can refer to MSF's website for more detailed updates – as Ms Denise Phua mentioned, you might have to do a few clicks but you can find all the details there – but today, let me share some key efforts and progress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, we want to empower persons with disabilities to pursue their work aspirations: to get a job and to stay employed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To do this, we adopt a person-centric approach, providing a range of employment support programmes to cater to various needs and capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SG Enable piloted the Place-and-Train programme in 2021, where employers receive salary support of up to 90% while they train persons with disabilities placed with them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The onsite team at EBH@Jurong also provides enhanced employment support for up to 24 months at a higher intensity, to support those with higher job support needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For some, the road to employment is a longer journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I recently met Lek Wei and his parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Lek Wei is autistic and often had meltdowns.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: After graduation, he enrolled as a Sheltered Workshop trainee with the Knead with Love bakery at the THK Pan-Disability Centre@Eunos.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The team provided a structured environment with routines, made efforts to understand how Lek Wei received instructions and gave him time and space when he was overwhelmed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He picked up skills like weighing ingredients and rolling dough and found joy in making delicious bread for others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Gradually, Lek Wei could regulate his emotions better and made such good progress that he secured a job trial at Boon Café@ITE College Central.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: During this trial period, the Sheltered Workshop and Job Coaches guided Boon Café in job redesigning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For example, Boon Café personalised Lek Wei's workstation by labelling the ingredients and colour coding the steps to his recipes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Café employees also learned how to communicate with him.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They speak to him slowly, with simple words.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through all these efforts, Lek Wei assimilated well and a few months later, Boon Café offered Lek Wei full-time employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Lek Wei was Boon Cafe's first employee with disability and he opened the door for the hiring of three more at the cafe.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I also tasted some of the pastry that he made, I must say they were "yummilicious".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han will be interested to know that our Sheltered Workshops provide a structured learning and training environment, with support from allied health professionals and training officers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As shown through Lek Wei, such environments enable those with higher needs to learn and develop at their own pace and hopefully, eventually enter open employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I am heartened, as Ms Carrie Tan and Ms Ng Ling Ling would be too, that more employers like Boon Café are hiring inclusively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These employers are accredited with the Enabling Mark.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Based on the Comprehensive Labour Force Survey for 2022 and 2023, close to half of persons with disabilities were employed in community, social and personal services, manufacturing and F&B services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To expand the jobs available, SG Enable is reaching out to employers in emerging sectors, such as transport and storage, including logistics; and financial and insurance services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We call upon more employers to be inclusive hirers, so that more people like Lek Wei can pursue their work aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond employers, the community plays a key role in enabling our persons with disabilities to live independently and feel valued.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the Enabling Masterplan, we committed to provide a continuum of support services that enable persons with disabilities to live in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will add 50 spaces to the MINDS Jurong Training and Development Centre by 2025, with the rest added progressively in the next few years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SG Enable launched the first Enabling Services Hub (ESH) in Tampines last August.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The ESH complements current support services by bringing services and programmes closer to homes of persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through working with community partners, we hope to create inclusive neighbourhoods and strengthen support for adults with disabilities and their caregivers, especially for those no longer actively receiving services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Take Irfan and his mother Mdm Sheriffa whom I met recently as well, for example.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Irfan was not suitable for work after graduation and was staying at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Thankfully, Sheriffa was connected to the ESH, which engaged Irfan in various activities close to where they stayed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One activity Irfan enjoys is volunteer book-shelving at the Tampines Regional Library.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So every Wednesday night, he hangs up his blue volunteer t-shirt, looking forward to volunteering the very next day.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Irfan also enjoys community fitness activities at Tampines West Community Club, including inclusive floorball activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These activities have brought Irfan out of isolation and into the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Irfan's engagement in activities allows Mdm Sheriffa to run errands or to have a much-needed respite before work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Sherrifa has also made friends with fellow caregivers through ESH activities and knows she is not alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To date, the first ESH has supported more than 140 persons with disabilities and caregivers living in Tampines and Bedok.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We hope that the ESHs will support more persons with disabilities like Irfan and very importantly, provide respite for caregivers like Mdm Sheriffa too.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I agree wholeheartedly with Mr Ong Hua Han that we need to support our caregivers, who play an indispensable role.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In fact, it is also a point that I made in my speech in the debate on the Budget statement just a week ago.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: CaringSG will collaborate with the ESH and other communities to strengthen community and peer support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To support persons with disabilities and their caregivers with long-term financial and care planning, more than 1,200 trust accounts have been set up with the Special Needs Trust Company, or SNTC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We share Mr Murali Pillai's hope that more families will set up trust accounts and tap on the Special Needs Saving Scheme (SNSS) to set aside Central Provident Fund (CPF) savings for long-term care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SNTC works with key partners, including SG Enable, SPED schools and social service agencies to reach out to families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Government is also strengthening support on caregiving costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For those who require point-to-point transport to commute to SPED schools and community-based programmes, we will increase the Enabling Transport Subsidy (ETS) from 1 April 2024 to alleviate the cost of transport services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Currently, about 5,400 beneficiaries are receiving the ETS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Valid means-test results can also be shared across schemes, so that beneficiaries need not undergo repeated means-testing within a period of time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will help ensure that our schemes and subsidies remain accessible to those who need them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Lastly, the EMP commits to improving accessibility and inclusiveness in our social and physical environments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have extensively improved the accessibility of our public transport and public spaces; all public buses and train stations and almost all public sector buildings are wheelchair-accessible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: You and I can play our part through small but impactful actions, such as looking out for those who need a hand, smiling more, staring less at unusual behaviour and focusing on their abilities and not limitations; because together, we can build a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):   Many citizens share similar aspirations for Singapore to be an inclusive and caring society, where everyone is empowered to pursue their own aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, let me share on how we are going to support lower-income families and PwDs to reach their full potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, ComLink+ reflects our philosophy in empowering lower-income families by encouraging action and progress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our family coaches journey with ComLink+ families through a family-centric approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The family coach will consider the family's circumstances, needs and strengths to co-develop an action plan with the family to achieve its goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Besides the volunteers that Minister mentioned, ComLink+ partners come from across the people, public and private sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our anchor partners, DBS, Singapore Pools and the Ngee Ann Kongsi have contributed generously towards supporting ComLink+ families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In this year of Celebrating Volunteers, I would like to thank ComLink+ befrienders for devoting your time and energy to journey with the families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Lower-income families and PwDs are often too saddled by today's burdens as they work towards achieving their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Government and social service partners adopt a person-centric and/or family-centric approach by providing a range of services and programmes to accommodate their various needs, capabilities and empower them to fulfil their potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Together, as a society, I hope that we can work together to create an inclusive and caring Singapore. : Sir, I started my speech asking whether Singapore can be a caring and inclusive place for all families, including our lower-income families and those with persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Aini, Lek Wei and Irfran have shown us, we can.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We can, when families do their best to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We can, when our social service partners and professionals journey alongside these families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We can, when our volunteers take time and energy to befriend our families and PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And we can, when you and I look out for those amongst us in need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is our refreshed social compact that we set out under Forward Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Together, we can create a caring and inclusive Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One where everyone can progress, fulfil their potential and achieve their aspirations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I have two supplementary questions, mostly for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The first one has to do with ComLink+.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I hear an almost picture-perfect narrative of what has happened.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: But I know and am sure the Senior Parliamentary Secretary also goes through quite a lot of this every day, that it is not picture-perfect and there are lots of challenges actually serving our families.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And I just want to reiterate what I asked in my cut.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And how do we intend to solve this?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And how do the rest of us, including the Government, plan to work at it together?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The second one has to do with the EMP for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Again, I want to ask from my cut.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: First is that it is great and I am very thankful for the report that was made.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: A lot of these reports pertain to the outputs, activities, and that is a really good start as well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: But we need to link it to outputs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: At the same time, we also want to make sure that it is not outdated.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Eight-year master plans are like really major things.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Even in this time and age, a lot of things, shelf lives are very short.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Also include what I shared about the need to include hot topics like inclusive insurance, criminal justice, review and strengthen the appropriate adult scheme and also to include ADHD and dyslexia, such neurodiverse conditions into our master plan.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And also, the hot button issues, which are really the financial subsidies for essential services, such as daily activity centres for those with moderate to severe disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I think we really need to consider a hybrid model of funding just like what we did many years ago, I think under Minister Vivian for MSF, where there is a universal core base and then you tap on, you add on, top up with means-tested subsidies so that at least the fundamental core expenses for such models can be covered.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Mr Eric Chua: I thank Ms Denise Phua for two very extensive clarifications.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I am afraid I will not be able to give a very detailed reply.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I agree with the Member that in terms of implementation, in fact, oftentimes, we meet a lot of implementation roadblocks, especially where we need partners to work together, especially where we need perhaps to push for maybe some flexibility at the edges of our current day policies.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: But rest assured that there is a very intentional view right from the social service officers on the ground, the SSOs' general managers, as well as each of the SSO officers that are in touch with the ComLink+ families, the family coaches, right up to the senior public servants, as well as myself.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: We do take a very keen interest in what is going on on the ground.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, that is a very broad answer to Ms Denise Phua's first question.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: To the second question, I want to thank her for being a very passionate advocate in this space.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And I assure the Member that we are not simply looking at output in the EMP.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And we are talking about going way beyond placements, because we do want persons with disabilities to keep their jobs, to sustain employment.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Because employment is not simply about having a job, having somewhere to go nine to six every day.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: It is also about self-actualisation in many instances.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, that is but one example of how outcomes are also being attended to.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And this is conducted once every two years.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: This is also one of those proxy reports that we refer to, to see how the needles are shifting in this space.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And I really want to behoove Ms Denise Phua that the EMP 2030 is not a dead plan.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: In fact, it is a very live plan.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: It does not mean that what we have said in 2022 is truth with a capital "T".

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: We are open to evolving some of the strategies; we are open to evolving some of the methods.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: In fact, we have stated in the Masterplan itself that we understand that things are changing, particularly in terms of, say, assistive technology.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And we acknowledge that and we welcome any suggestions along the way as we get to 2030.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And if I can add, 2030 is most definitely not a full stop.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: To me, it is the figurative comma in our journey towards making Singapore a more inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I hope that is sufficient assurance for the Member.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: I am very happy to hear that the National Family Week will now be extended to a month-long festival.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: This will certainly allow for more families to participate and also for more family-oriented programmes to be included.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: My question is really regarding the lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Perhaps, the FFL can work with SSA, family coaches, even the People's Association, to maybe bring the ComLink+ families to participate in these activities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: My second question is for Minister of State Sun Xueling.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Given the recent spate of incidents involving the preschool sector, what can MSF and ECDA do to assure parents on the safety and standards of our preschools?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Were these incidents a result of insufficient resources deployed by the preschools?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: If so, what can ECDA do to ensure that all our preschools are adequately resourced?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And I hope that when we do the National Family Festival, it is not something that is top-down, something that FFL does or MSF does, but also for grassroots organisations, corporates to participate, whether or not they get reported in media or otherwise, because I think when this festivity goes on throughout Singapore, and then, like what Mr Yong was mentioning just now, get everyone involved, whether they are disabled or from a needy family, I think this will augur well for what Singapore is about, an inclusive and caring society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we do have to get a ground-up initiative.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We want to have ideas, what can be done.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just to give Members an example I tried in my own Community Club where we have a simple two-hour sit-down family chillax.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just everyone can come and we just charge $5.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I have a little surplus in my Community Club, I say let us spend and give families a good time.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But for the families which are living in rentals, who we know are in the ComLink+ or other programmes, we get the befrienders as well as SSOs to tell us who they are, invite them and charge them maybe just $1.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Because they have to show they have a ticket.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And I do not think free is always good, to show that they will be committed to come.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But when they came, we did not know, we did not identify so-and-so was needy, so-and-so was disabled.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Everyone was just sitting around having a chill time and it was a great atmosphere.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, it does not have to be very structured.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just have a band play for them from five to seven, food truck, free flow of food, that kind of festivity I think will be very welcomed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, I hope that corporates, whether you do it on-site or as a family day outing, extend this to other families who may be needy, as part of corporate responsibility, too.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And we have not observed that these were contravened.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And I think it is a strong reminder to the industry that teachers need to be accountable for their actions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They need to know that they will be swiftly taken to task if they are found to be errant or negligent and that centre leaders have to be responsible and that they have to supervise.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The last point I would like to add is that, as I mentioned in my speech earlier, the current levers that ECDA has is limited by our current set of legislation in place.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I have just two clarifications, one for Minister of State Sun Xueling and one for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: For the pilot infant childminding services, can the Minister of State share more about which part of Singapore will the pilot be implemented?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: What are the fees that young parents can expect?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Will the subsidy be the same as the current infant care for licensed centres?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Also, how will the quality and safety standards be checked, especially if they are not done on centre-based?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: For Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua, the question is on the family coaches for ComLink+.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I think it is an excellent idea to roll out this initiative.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: How do we help them, especially if the caseload can be about 25 to 35 families for each family coach?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: First and foremost, this is a pilot nationwide.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we are not specific about where the pilot locations are.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But that said, we are currently engaging operators.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It depends on which operators see it as a viable business model and the operators may also have their own geographical focus areas.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, what I would like to say is that it is not intentional from MSF as to where the pilots would be.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But depending on who are the operators who are interested in working with MSF on this, we could see a situation whereby we could start in certain locations first rather than others, but it is a function of which are the interested operators.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We just want to make sure that this is affordable and is seen as a flexible childminding option for parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The last question that she had was with regard to standards.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I shared that we would have established processes for incident management because we understand from parents, that safety is very important to them should they wish to consider this option and we will also ensure that childminders undergo basic training in areas, such as basic infant care, first aid training, food safety and hygiene.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Indeed, we do need the right type for a family coach and basically, we look for a few things.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: One, is a person somebody who really is passionate and really genuine and authentic about helping people from lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Two, somebody who can display empathy and have good, strong communication and interpersonal skills because that will be helpful when communicating some of the action plans or things that the families need to work on.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And three, really, individuals with good analytical planning, as well as problem-solving skills.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, we are also open to having mid-career switchers join us because we do understand that mid-career switchers, they have more working and family experience and a lot of time this will come in useful.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Because we are talking about life experiences that the family coach could potentially share with the families that they work with.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But in addition to the type of candidates that we are looking for our family coaches, we also provide a comprehensive suite of training.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: There is a structured training programme for family coaches before they are deployed and at various milestone stages and this will include frameworks that they can use to assess the family's strengths and needs for action planning and also engagement-related training.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, things like basic counselling, motivational interviewing, cultural competency as well as coaching techniques; and also working effectively with stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Because it is not about just bringing a goodie bag or a bag of different schemes to the families.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is about connecting the family to other agencies, other organisations on the ground, so there needs to be a good sense of who these partners are going to be and a good team spirit or team player-ship, if you will, in working with the partners on the ground.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, these are all the qualities that we look at and try to nurture and imbue in our family coaches.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: I have a clarification for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: Does MSF or SG Enable actively track and engage those who successfully graduate from the Sheltered Workshop-to-Work Programme, say after one or two years, to ensure that they do not fall back into unemployment or sheltered workshops a few years post-transition?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, I do not have the numbers on hand as to how many of PwDs drop out after one year and at the different milestone times, but rest assured that the passion as well as the appetite to really look at helping a PwD, not just land the job, but to really sustain and remain in employment is there.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: To clarify whether I heard correctly that, she mentioned there will be some training provided for parents under the EIPIC programme if they have children with advanced or high developmental needs?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And the reason why we want to do so is that the international studies have shown that parents, they are the early educators, early role models in their children's lives and they are in the best position to embed intervention related to social, emotional skills.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, just think about it in terms of percentage terms, this is already a very, very large increase.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And what that means, obviously, is that we have to bring in more professionals into the space; but we are also extremely mindful that these professionals will obviously have to be adequately-trained and they would also have to be aware of the norms that we have in our society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And very importantly, to be able to work with our parents; the parents of these children with developmental needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, where there are specific specialisations, for instance, it could be speech therapy, could be play therapy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Where possible, we would look at bringing in international staff to cope with and to be helpful.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But I think we would like to keep a core group of educators in Singapore and we will definitely be training more of these educators because it is important that we are able to take care of these children with developmental needs, with educators who are trained in Singapore and who are trusted by our parents here in Singapore.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I know Mr Giam you have raised your hands several times.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I had given priority to those who had filed cuts first.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I am very glad to hear that MSF is planning to professionalise and subsidise childminding services.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, my question for Minister of State Sun Xueling is, can I ask how this will affect existing informal childminders?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I have residents who look after their neighbours' infants and kids after school and these are usually older women who are not highly educated and may not be prepared to be formally employed by childminding operators.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, they may have difficulties completing formal courses and passing written tests.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, how will these informal childminders and the parents who engage their services, be able to tap on the subsidies that MSF is offering under this programme?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our intent is to have more options for parents, which means that if there is an existing arrangement between a nanny or an infant childminder in the community with a parent, we are not going to go in there and change the arrangements.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But because we are launching a pilot and when we launch a pilot, we do hope that the results from that pilot will guide us in being able to have it more as a permanent programme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we have to make sure then that the parameters are such that it is sustainable and, therefore, we will need to have certain standards in place.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, what I would say is: in the situation that you mentioned, whatever is an informal arrangement right now – if it is something that they are happy with and there is something ongoing, it is something that they have been doing for a long time between the parent and the infant childminder, they can just go ahead with whatever it is that they have right now.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But if they should want to be able to be part of this pilot so that the parent is able to make use of the subsidies that the Government is providing, then we would require the childminder to adhere to the standards that I have shared earlier.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is also so that MSF is responsible for the pilot and then we know what are the parameters that would make this work.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I believe Minister Masagos mentioned earlier that the ComLink+ family coaches are actually social workers from the FSCs and I believe the Minister is aware of the already heavy workload of FSCs' social workers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, I would like to ask whether MSF will actually be able to provide additional resources and funding to FSCs, so that FSCs are sufficiently equipped?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The families who live in rental homes who have children, part of them are already under the FSC.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, they have a relationship with the FSC social worker and this is not an additional job for them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is to let them do their work even better because we give them more tools to incentivise their families to achieve their lifelong goals, in addition to resolving issues like divorce or family violence and so forth.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, I do not see this as an additional burden to them but actually they would very much welcome that now they have more tools to enable them to achieve the objectives that they want for these families.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Just to clarify with the Minister of State, can existing individual childminders join the programme or do they have to be employed by a childminding operator?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I just want to make a clarification to my main speech earlier.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If not, can I invite Mr Melvin Yong, if you like, to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: We have learned that there can never be a silver bullet that would resolve the overlapping problems that distress family faces, but I am heartened that MSF and the social service sector are doing their best to support and to help vulnerable Singaporeans and foster a caring society.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Their work is often unseen but crucial and commendable.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Chairman, with that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.40 pm.

text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 4.17 pm until 4.40 pm.
